title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is §2 of the continuation of the Longue Marche, titled 'Enveloppes schématiques des L-groupes', part 1° 'Notion de L-groupe … (cas discret)'.

Groupe à lacets. A 'groupe à lacets' of type (g,ν) is the fundamental group π of a surface X∖S of finite construction, where X is compact orientable of genus g and S is a finite set of ν points. It comes with its 'loop subgroups': the conjugacy classes of inertia subgroups ≅ Z around the punctures.

Previous page. Grothendieck observed that a finite-index subgroup π_0 inherits a loop structure, by intersecting the loop subgroups of π with π_0. Geometrically this is pulling back to a finite covering. He also noted the low cases g=0, ν∈{0,1} where the loop structure is not given just by conjugacy classes of Z-subgroups.

This page, step by step.
(i) He finishes the bracket on the exceptional cases: (0,1), with a marginal insertion about π≅Z, and (0,0), where π={1} and π_0=π.
(ii) Conversely, the loop structure of π is recovered from the structures of its finite-index subgroups π_0 (when they exist). The loop subgroups of π are the centralizers in π of the loop subgroups of π_0. In the hyperbolic case this is correct: the centralizer of a parabolic element is the maximal parabolic infinite cyclic subgroup.
(iii) Let π be a discrete group. Let L_0(π) be the set of loop-group structures on π of 'admissible' type, i.e. type ≠ (0,1), (0,0), and an inserted (1,0). This essentially imposes non-degeneracy, close to 2g−2+ν>0.
(iv) For finite-index subgroups π_i, restriction makes the L_0(π_i) an inductive system of sets.
(v) A first attempt, L(π) = lim L_0(π_i), is crossed out. It is replaced by (1): L_0^G(π_i) = the set of loop structures on a normal finite-index π_i that are invariant under the finite group G_i = π/π_i.
(vi) If some finite-index π_{i0} has L(π_{i0}) ≠ ∅, then π_{i0} is finitely generated, hence so is π. He deduces that normal finite-index subgroups are cofinal among finite-index subgroups.
(vii) 'On pose alors' leads to the next page's definition: L(π) = colim over normal finite-index π_i of L_0^{G_i}(π_i).

What it serves. An L-structure is a germ (commensurability class) of G-invariant surface-group-with-punctures structures on finite-index normal subgroups. This is exactly the data of the orbifold fundamental group of a 2-orbifold of finite type: a Fuchsian group of finite covolume together with its cusp subgroups. It is introduced so as to include 'groupes fondamentaux mixtes' of surfaces with finite automorphism groups. The aim is then to construct schematic (pro-algebraic) envelopes of such groups.
errors: The cofinality of normal finite-index subgroups among finite-index subgroups does not need finite generation. For any group, the normal core of a finite-index subgroup has finite index. Finite generation matters only for countability, or for cofinality of characteristic subgroups.

The list of excluded types is ambiguous. (0,1) and (0,0) both have trivial π. The marginal 'dans π≃Z' suggests the problematic Z case (sphere minus 2 points, type (0,2)), which is not clearly listed among the exclusions. With (1,0) inserted, the intended condition appears to be hyperbolicity (2g−2+ν>0), but (0,2) is not visibly excluded.

Recovering loop subgroups as centralizers requires the hyperbolic case. In Euclidean cases such as the torus, centralizers are the whole group, so the exclusion of (1,0) is needed for this step too. This is not stated.

ideas.what: Group with a loop structure (peripheral structure) on surface groups of type (g,ν); induction to finite-index subgroups by intersection
ideas.modern_name: peripheral structure / surface group pair; Fuchsian group with cusp subgroups
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Fricke–Klein, Nielsen); in Grothendieck's framework, Longue Marche 1981
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981, circulated); Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Recovering the loop structure of π from that of a finite-index subgroup via centralizers of loop subgroups
ideas.modern_name: maximal parabolic subgroups as centralizers / commensurators of parabolics

ideas.what: L-structure defined as a colimit over normal finite-index subgroups of G-invariant loop structures, i.e. a germ of structure up to commensurability, making orbifold groups (with torsion) into 'L-groups'
ideas.modern_name: orbifold fundamental groups of 2-orbifolds of finite type; virtually-surface groups (Nielsen realization, Eckmann–Müller–Zieschang)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thurston (orbifolds, ~1978); Zieschang, Eckmann–Müller (virtual surface groups); Kerckhoff (Nielsen realization 1983)

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines orbifold-type fundamental groups intrinsically, as germs of invariant loop structures over the cofinal system of normal finite-index subgroups. He does this rather than via orbifold charts, in preparation for 'schematic envelopes' (pro-algebraic completions) of such groups. It is a clean commensurability-invariant formalism, but its content is equivalent to known results on Fuchsian/virtually-surface groups.
missed.quote: L_0^G(π_i) = ens des structures à lacets sur π_i invariants par G_i = π/π_i
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mild documentary interest. It is the setup for pro-algebraic or relative completions of orbifold groups (cf. Hain's relative completion of mapping class groups) within Grothendieck's anabelian programme. The definitions themselves are not new.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is foundational definitional work: loop structures on finite-index subgroups and a colimit definition of L-structures that amounts to orbifold fundamental groups. It is natural and correct up to minor points, and its mathematical content is known; the novelty lies only in the formalism and its intended use toward schematic envelopes.
transcription_corrections: 'sous-groupes lacets de π étant les intersections pour [?] π des sous-groupes-lacets de π_0' should read roughly 'les sous-groupes lacets de π étant les centralisateurs dans π des sous-groupes-lacets de π_0'. The image shows 'centralisateurs', not 'intersections'.
'celles des π_{0,i}' is probably just 'celles des π_0' (with a subscript), i.e. the loop structures of the finite-index subgroups.
'P. ex [-les-] sous-groupes [-des-] π_i' is more likely 'Pour les sous-groupes π_i de π, d'indice fini, les L_0(π_i) forment un système inductif d'ensembles'.
The final sentence should read: 'il s'ensuit que l'ens. des sous-groupes distingués d'indice fini est cofinal dans l'ens des sous-groupes d'indice fini'.
The crossed-out passage contains 'S'il existe un π_{i0} d'indice fini tel que … syst. générateur fini', which was rewritten below it.
